A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, despite the changed title and renaming of ARM to RAD-Q and RAD to RAD-V. All 24 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables for comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original detoxification and sentiment-control experiments, synthetic expressivity tests, matrix-factorization results, ablations and decoding-time measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and reports additional loss/head comparisons, a DExperts parameter sweep and revised matrix-completion experiments.

M1.justification: The default architecture, squared-loss training, distillation, baseline regularization and decoding procedure remain unchanged after renaming. Appendix G.2 adds experimental variants using cross-entropy with sigmoid-transformed predictions and a nonlinear MLP reward head.

E1.justification: The natural-language datasets and tasks are retained. The synthetic expressivity scenario changes from a fully observed 1024-by-1024 identity matrix in v2 Appendix C.1 to partially observed triangular constraints in v3 Appendix D.1, testing expressivity when rewards are missing.

E2.justification: The external baseline roster is retained, and DExperts was already evaluated in v2. Appendix G.2 adds explicit comparison variants—cross-entropy-trained RAD-Q and RAD-Q+MLP—against the retained squared-loss, linear model.

E3.justification: The main generation protocols remain unchanged. Matrix completion changes from 50 iterations with penalty 0.01 followed by 50 without penalty to 1000 iterations with penalty 0.0001 and several specified ranks. New DExperts and model-variant comparisons use 1000 randomly selected prompts with top-k=20; the synthetic test also changes its observation mask.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands supplementary validation: Figures 9–11 test DExperts across control strengths, squared loss versus cross-entropy, and linear versus MLP heads. Appendices C–D also expand rank-dependent data-fitting analysis and revise the synthetic expressivity test. The earlier regularization/baseline ablation and classifier checks are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, repeated-training-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3 elaborates on the existing random-prefix rank estimation but introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The benchmark numbers in v2 Tables 2–6 match v3 Tables 3–7. New Table 2 reports dataset-specific completion errors, including 4.7e-7 and 6.6e-7 at rank 767 under revised fitting settings. Synthetic results are replaced under changed observation conditions. Figures 9–11 newly report a better trade-off than DExperts, a slight advantage for squared loss, and similar linear/MLP performance.

T1.justification: v3 introduces minimum completion rank and its numerical counterpart, revising the expressivity criterion previously expressed using the zero-filled matrix's rank. It adds a single-missing-value lemma, a full-rank triangular counterexample and a formal row-reduction lemma. The new probability-one claim in Lemma 1 and Appendix C.2 requires stronger distributional assumptions than stated.

C1.justification: v2 primarily presents ARM as an efficient reward model motivated by observed low ranks. v3 makes the general Q-style versus V-style expressivity distinction, and cases where low-rank parametrization is insufficient, central contributions in the introduction and conclusion. The efficiency and benchmark-quality claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 conjectures that deterministic, averaged teacher targets explain distillation's advantage, attributes the DExperts gap to training objectives, and recommends linear heads based on the new ablation. The earlier toxicity-safety and potentially high-rank toxicity limitations remain present in Appendix A.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents the matrix-completion optimization objective and revised iteration/penalty settings, and expands numerical-rank cutoff and sampling explanations. The existing model initialization, frozen embeddings, Adam settings, learning rates, epochs, hardware and model-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the work through reinforcement-learning Q/V and dueling-network connections, adding discussion of works including Han, Mudgal, Chakraborty and Xu. Section 5 distinguishes its finite-dimensional rank analysis from GenARM's universal-approximator argument, extending the earlier guided-decoding positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and substantial portions of the introduction and related work are rewritten around parametrization choices. Section 3.1 becomes four structured subsections, terminology changes throughout, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. This exceeds a simple model renaming.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the earlier ARM illustration with a RAD-V/RAD-Q architecture comparison, adds reward-matrix diagrams, a rank-error table and three comparison plots. Retained top-k=40 curves are separated into appendix figures, and typography, figure sizing and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the central rationale by distinguishing minimum completion rank from zero-filled matrix rank and adds useful tests of loss, head architecture and DExperts control strength. However, the main benchmark results remain unchanged, and the new probability-one lemma relies on an insufficient full-support assumption. The clearer argument and targeted validation provide a limited net improvement, tempered by this theoretical defect.
